founder.name: Maria Chen
founder.notes: 10 years multi-unit restaurant operations; most recently Director of Operations for a 42-unit QSR franchise group in the Texas Triangle. Left that role 3 months ago. No stated funding strategy yet.

business_basics.one_liner: Software that lets a multi-location restaurant's shift manager automatically text the right qualified backup workers the moment someone calls out sick, so the shift gets covered in minutes instead of the manager working down a phone list for 45 minutes while the line backs up.
business_basics.business_type_notes: B2B SaaS, hybrid self-serve/sales-led: a single-location GM can self-serve a trial, but real revenue is sales-assisted contracts signed at the multi-unit franchise-group level. Buyer (Director of Operations / Owner-Operator) and day-to-day user (shift manager/GM) are different people. Must integrate with existing scheduling systems (7shifts, HotSchedules named by founder). SMS delivery is a hard requirement, not push notification, because backup workers often don't have the employer's scheduling app installed.

01_market_segmentation.summary: 15 candidate segments identified; shortlisted for Step 2: QSR franchise groups (10-50 units), casual-dining chains, convenience-store retail, home health aide agencies, school districts

02_select_a_beachhead_market.summary: Beachhead selected: QSR franchise groups, 10-50 units, single metro/region — highest score on reach and right-to-win via founder's own network

03_build_an_end_user_profile.summary: End user profile drafted from 3 real conversations: GM/shift manager at one location of a 10-50 unit QSR group, no budget authority, measured on labor cost % and on-time-opening

04_calculate_the_tam_for_the_beachhead_m.summary: Bottom-up beachhead TAM = $118M/year (66,000 locations x $1,788/year); source: founder estimate, unvalidated group count

05_profile_the_persona_for_the_beachhead.summary: Persona: Jordan Vasquez, GM at a 14-unit QSR group — grounded in real interview

06_full_life_cycle_use_case.summary: Full life cycle mapped across 8 stages for Jordan Vasquez; biggest drop-off risk: onboarding/first use

07_high_level_product_specification.summary: 6 Must-have capabilities defined, traced to the FLCUC; core flow: SMS call-out broadcast, first-accept-wins, target 8 min time-to-cover

08_quantify_the_value_proposition.summary: Quantified value = ~$6,000/yr per location vs. status quo call list; gap judged marginal-to-sufficient, resting on an unproven 8-minute target

09_identify_your_next_10_customers.summary: 7 of 10 real prospects identified; beachhead accessibility: partially validated (network depth thinner than Step 2's reach score implied)

10_define_your_core.summary: Core: cross-location reliability-data pool (design bet, not yet earned); resulting advantages: faster time-to-cover, multi-group pool draw; verdict: moat only today, not yet a true core

11_chart_your_competitive_position.summary: Axes: speed of coverage vs cross-location reach; position: fast+cross-location target position currently unoccupied (unverified); defensibility: contestable until Core exists

12_determine_the_dmu.summary: DMU mapped: ~2-3 distinct roles typical; champion = ambiguous, economic buyer = Director of Operations. Revision cycle (2026-08-25): 3 of 7 Step 9 prospects called re: franchisor veto — 2 of 3 clear, 1 of 3 has a non-fatal security-review requirement; partial confirmation, not full.

13_map_the_process_to_acquire_a_paying_c.summary: 6-stage acquisition path mapped; riskiest stage: franchisor IT/brand-standards check (Stage 4), brand-dependent. Revision cycle (2026-08-25): Stage 4's binary-veto framing softened per Step 12's partial confirmation; blended time/conversion figures not yet recomputed.

14_calculate_the_tam_for_follow_on_marke.summary: Pin 2 (casual dining) TAM = $70.8M/yr, founder estimate; Pin 3 (convenience retail) not sized — no basis yet

15_design_a_business_model.summary: Selected model: per-location monthly subscription sold at the franchise-group level; freemium/usage-based/take-rate rejected as DMU- or compliance-mismatched

16_set_your_pricing_framework.summary: Pricing: $149/location/month standard, $129/location/month volume tier (11+ locations); untested with real prospects

17_calculate_the_ltv_of_a_customer.summary: Blended LTV = $52,503 per signed group contract (22-location avg, $129/mo volume tier, 74% margin, 25-month lifetime); all inputs low confidence, unmeasured

18_map_the_sales_process_to_acquire_a_cu.summary: Sales cycle ~68 days, 3.6% aware-to-signed conversion, ~37.8 founder-hours per closed customer; entirely warm-network-sourced, no paid channel modeled. Revision cycle (2026-08-25): real pipeline status logged (2 of 7 prospects at Stage 2, council's 5+ bar not yet met) — funnel figures deliberately NOT recomputed from an insufficient sample; council required revision [SALES-CYCLE] remains open.

19_calculate_the_coca.summary: COCA = $3,213/customer, LTV:COCA ~16.3:1, 1.5-month payback — flagged as misleadingly optimistic since it excludes any paid/scalable channel. Revision cycle (2026-08-25): one real 20-contact cold-outbound test run (15% reply rate) per council required revision [SCALABILITY]; logged as a directional data point, not used to recompute COCA/ratio (sample too small).

20_identify_key_assumptions.summary: 29-item register swept from Steps 1-19; 8 ranked leap-of-faith assumptions identified, top 3: unproven value-prop target, non-scalable warm-network COCA, onboarding adoption risk

21_test_key_assumptions.summary: All 8 leap-of-faith assumptions deferred (idea stage, no MVBP live yet); biggest open risk carried forward: cross-location pool assumption is testable today at zero cost and has not been tested

22_define_the_mvbp.summary: MVBP: SMS broadcast + first-accept-wins for one pilot group at full price ($129-149/location/mo), manual onboarding, success = 3 real call-outs covered in 30 days

23_show_that_dogs_will_eat_the_dog_food.summary: No usage evidence exists yet — no MVBP customer sold. Honest read: not yet measurable.

24_develop_a_product_plan.summary: Roadmap gated on MVBP shipping + cross-location-pool test. Revision cycle (2026-08-25): council required revision [EXECUTION-RISK] addressed — real, time-boxed engineering-resourcing decision made (no-code solo attempt, 2-week checkpoint, funded contractor fallback), replacing the prior open gap.

key_assumptions.test_plan: Ask this directly in the next 10 backup-worker conversations (feeds Step 9); if resistance is high, the beachhead may need to narrow to single-owner multi-location groups only, not cross-owner pools.
